_desc: Phase-3 routing-liveness gate — the NO-ALT active rediscovery (the user's real bug: a dest reachable ONLY via a DEPARTED relay, with NO passive alt). LINE topology alice-bob-carol: bob is alice's SOLE next-hop to carol (relayed in bob's first beacons). bob then DEPARTS — forced_drops kill EVERY bob->alice frame from the 4th occurrence on (after the first 3 beacons establish carol-via-bob), so bob stops CTS/ACKing alice's RTS. alice's DMs to carol fail at bob; the failed flights are liveness evidence -> bob crosses suspect (2 timeouts) then SILENT (3). With the SOLE candidate (bob) now silent and NO alt, Phase 3 fires an RREQ (r_tx, reason=no_route) to actively rediscover a path instead of silently re-RTSing the dead bob until the 3 h aging TTL (the pre-Phase-3 stall — the exact failure mode behind the user's persistent stale-via-191 route). No alt path EXISTS here, so delivery cannot recover — the gate proves the ACTIVE-REDISCOVERY REACTION (suspect-mark + RREQ), not recovery. (RREQ-driven recovery is covered deterministically by the native §P3 unit test; a multi-node recovery sim is blocked by the F-frame-labelled-as-BCN telemetry gap + DV passive route propagation — see the phase report.) Idle + lossless otherwise (sigma_db=0). NB: an empty forced_drops `label` matches ALL frame labels (SimController.cpp), modelling bob's full departure.
